title: 3-238th Aviation Regiment Soldiers support Hurricane Helene relief mission (No GFX)
description:
Soldiers from Company B, 3rd Battalion, 238th Aviation Regiment deploy to North Carolina to support Hurricane Helene recovery efforts in October 2024. National Guard units from 17 states responded to areas impacted by the storm and took part in food and water distribution, search and rescue, debris clearance and other tasks as needed. (U.S. Army National Guard video by Staff Sgt. Thomas Moeger, Ohio National Guard Public Affairs)

Interview 1: Capt. Zachary Johnson, commander, Company B, 3rd Battalion, 238th Aviation
Regiment

Interview 2: Staff Sgt. Derrick Bauman, flight engineer, Company B, 3rd Battalion, 238th
Aviation Regiment

Interview 3: Sgt. Garrett Tester, flight engineer, Company B, 3rd Battalion, 238th Aviation
Regiment

Interview 4: Chief Warrant Officer 2 Joseph Looby, CH-47 Chinook helicopter pilot, Company
B, 3rd Battalion, 238th Aviation Regiment

transcript.text: So when we got the call to come up on
state active duty for the Hurricane
Helene mission , it became very
apparent very quickly that this need
was going to be immense and that they
needed crews from wherever they can get
it . We can go out and do training
flights and stuff like that , which
typically prepare us for deployments ,
but back home it's nice to be able to
help out , you know , actual people
that you live with or even in other
states in this case , you know , where
the needs back home , it's nice . To be
a part of that . We flew about a
quarter of our hours in 2 weeks that we
flew on a 9 month deployment that the
unit was on , uh , a few years back .
So to cram that much flight time into a
2.5 week period was pretty intense . We
were doing 12 to 14 hour days every day ,
moving a lot of cargo . So total
reverse of what I was expecting . I was ,
I was expecting there was a chance we
went down there and didn't do anything
and we , we worked our butts off . The
most rewarding part of this mission was
honestly just at the end of the day
being able to help people . This was a
legitimate cost . People really needed
these supplies , needed help , um ,
from where they're at , and to be able
to do our actual mission and make a
difference was the most rewarding thing
I've done so far in my career with the
Ohio National Guard .
